newsitem.title: DENMARK: THREE WOUNDED IN DANISH BIKER SHOOTING.
newsitem.headline: THREE WOUNDED IN DANISH BIKER SHOOTING.

text.p: Gunmen shot and wounded three men connected to the Bandidos motorcycle gang on Monday in what appeared to be a fresh eruption of a long-smouldering Nordic biker war that has killed eight people throughout the region.
Police in the town of Aalborg, in the north of Denmark's Jutland peninsula, said that the wounded men were in a red Peugeot car which had stopped at a crossroads when a Fiat drew up alongside them.

"Witnesses said that passengers in the two vehicles shouted at each other through the windows, then suddenly a heavy handweapon was drawn and several shots were fired toward the red car," Chief Inspector Preben Juel Hansen told TV2 television.
One of the men was seriously injured, the television said.
Police suspect the attack was carried out by the Bandidos' bitter rivals, the Hells Angels, but had no immediate evidence.
The vendetta between the two gangs has festered since Bandidos first began to challenge Hells Angels' dominance in the summer of 1993.
A member of the Hells Angels-affiliated Rednecks died in a gunfight with Bandidos in Sweden in 1994 and two Bandidos were slain over the following two years in Sweden and Finland.
Full-scale war erupted in March 1996 when gunmen outside Copenhagen airport shot dead Danish Bandido leader Uffe Larsen and wounded three of his companions.

A Danish Bandidos member was fatally shot in the head near the Norwegian town of Drammen in July the same year and in October, in an apparent act of revenge, a shoulder fired missile ploughed into Hells Angels headquarters in Copenhagen, killing a member and a women party guest.
The most recent fatality was in Aalborg, where Hells Angel Kim Svendsen was shot dead last January.
Danish Queen Margrethe was on a visit to the town when Monday's shooting took place, but was safely on the royal yacht in the town's harbour at the time.
